prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No self-cleaning, dust-proof panel is deployed at scale, so the Main KPI of 300,000 MW of desert solar with no water cleaning is not met by the project's approach. The panel-intrinsic routes remain research: MIT's electrostatic dust removal (2022, patent pending, no commercial launch found, https://www.technologyreview.com/2022/04/27/1048479/a-better-way-to-clean-solar-panels), electrodynamic screens with small field trials only (Sol Clarity, 11 panels; Brunel 2025 simulation, https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/handle/2438/33024), and anti-soiling coatings whose multi-year desert durability is unproven (CSU thesis, https://mountainscholar.org/handle/10217/195368). Honest limit: the 'no water' half of the KPI is partly answered by deployed waterless robotic cleaning (Ecoppia, about 99% dust removal claimed, https://www.pv-tech.org/news/ecoppia-installs-cleaning-robots-for-40mw-solar-plant-on-israel-jordan-bord; Noor Abu Dhabi's 1,430 dry robots, https://noorabudhabi.ae/plants/robotic-cleaning-system/). I found no total for GW served by waterless robots and cannot rule out that it is a large fraction of MENA desert PV; it is not shown to reach 300 GW. Tasks must not reward re-inventing waterless robots and must target durable panel-intrinsic dust rejection with their own prior-art basis.
